why.cutoff_c: one thermal limit, at 90 C: the owner's decision
why.datasheet_derate_speed: this servo never turns faster than two thirds of the no-load speed the maker of its class states, written as the ratio 2 over 3: the speed ceiling, which protects the brushes. A decision for this servo and no rule for another: the owner's decision
why.datasheet_derate_default: any other value taken from the maker's sheet is taken at 0.8 of it on this servo, to be safe; no rule reads it yet. A decision for this servo and no rule for another: the owner's decision
why.datasheet_speed_voltage: the maker's sheet states a range of operating voltage, 4.8 V to 6.6 V, and a no-load speed at two voltages of it, so the ceiling takes the speed stated at the stated voltage nearest the rail this servo runs on, the registry's rated_v: on 5.0 V that is the 4.8 V row, 600 deg/s, and the ceiling is 400 deg/s. The 6.0 V row, 750 deg/s, would give 500 deg/s and is not taken: the owner chose 400 deg/s, a speed measured not to damage the brushes. A decision for this servo and no rule for another: the owner's decision
why.winding_plateau_reading: the high reading of the winding's plateau over the board NTC, the earlier model's two modes together: of the two readings it alone reads at least as hot as the set the servo holds in every case computed, heating, pulsed and cooling, so the step loosens nothing. The plateau is not graded on this pair, and the lock hold at 0.25 A decides later: the owner's decision
why.thermal_tau2_s: the family's slow mode, quoted from earlier work on another servo of the type, until a lock hold with its cooling measures this motor's: the owner's decision
why.th_rise2_q016: the family's slow gain at the reading winding_plateau_reading names, on this motor's own resistance and counts per A, until a lock hold measures this motor's plateau: the owner's decision
why.i_cont_ma: interim, until the lock hold gives this motor's plateau: the owner's decision
why.stall_release_ma: it moves with the continuous current, interim with it: the owner's decision
why.collision_trip: the collision trip stays off: the owner's decision
why.hold_band_floor_counts: the hold band is 4 counts, a bit of hunting after a landing is fine while it dies down quickly: the owner's decision
why.stall_response: a blocked horn folds to the continuous current and recovers on the next command, as the Feetech class does, and the 90 C cutoff is the backstop: the owner's decision
why.stall_time_ms: on a free horn the stall conditions never last past 12 ms, and the Feetech class allows 2 s; interim until the load arm: the owner's decision
why.stall_omega_max_deg_s: four times the speed noise of a still shaft, at the speed the servo's counts are on the set's count: the owner's decision
why.pos_error_deg: twice the worst healthy following error on record, 4.4 deg on a free horn; interim until the load arm confirms it: the owner's decision
why.pos_error_time_ms: a healthy error never holds that long, and a reversed motor is caught before it reaches a stop; interim with the angle: the owner's decision
why.sensor_delta_max_counts: twice the worst healthy pot step on 5 V, 32 counts: the owner's decision
why.sensor_bad_samples: the default stands: no capture shows a failing pot, and a capture of one would revisit it: the owner's decision
why.v_undervolt_v: 0.25 V over the edge the rail walk of 2026-11-14 found, where the chip's supply, the ADC's reference, leaves regulation and the rail reading stops falling, for the 5 V bench supply; a 2S pack's floor waits for the pack on the board: the owner's decision
why.rail_source_ohm: designed for a soft supply such as a battery on a long lead; a stiffer setting protects less, and it never acts on the 5 V bench supply: the owner's decision
why.duty_max_share: no voltage cap: the speed ceiling and the current limit protect the motor: the owner's decision
why.oc_trip_ma: a wiring or bridge fault detector: above the locked-rotor current on a full 2S pack, about 2.0 A, so only a short reaches it: the owner's decision
why.oc_trip_samples: it rides over single-sample spikes, 0.4 ms: the owner's decision
why.openloop_decay: the off-time brake: smooth current, torque in proportion to duty: the owner's decision
why.openloop_zero_brake: zero duty coasts in open loop, which calibration relies on: the owner's decision
why.gear_ratio_centi: the family's tooth count, to be confirmed by counting this unit's teeth: the owner's decision
why.v_kp_q88: its counts stay as benched, they have run on the table since rung 12a-pos-table-live: the owner's decision
why.v_ki_q412: its counts stay as benched, they have run on the table since rung 12a-pos-table-live: the owner's decision
